ne-2e30cb21.stem: Which almond-shaped nucleus deep in the temporal lobe plays the main role in processing fear and emotional responses?
ne-2e30cb21.explanation: The amygdala is part of the limbic system; it is involved in detecting danger, in fear and in forming emotional memories. It lies just in front of the hippocampus.

ne-e1589513.stem: Through which group of nuclei are all senses except smell relayed before reaching the cortex?
ne-e1589513.explanation: The thalamus is the largest part of the diencephalon; vision, hearing, taste and body sensation are relayed in its nuclei and sent on to the corresponding cortical areas. The olfactory pathway reaches the cortex without passing through the thalamus.

ne-ee3fb626.stem: Which structure regulates body temperature, hunger and thirst, and pituitary secretion?
ne-ee3fb626.explanation: The hypothalamus forms the floor of the third ventricle and the lower part of its side walls. By controlling the autonomic system and the pituitary it maintains the balance of the internal environment (homeostasis).

ne-da4674e1.stem: Which structure produces most of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?
ne-da4674e1.explanation: CSF is produced mostly in the choroid plexuses of the ventricles (about 500 ml a day). The arachnoid granulations reabsorb the CSF into the venous sinuses.

ne-a7eeee6f.stem: Which opening connects the lateral ventricles with the third ventricle?
ne-a7eeee6f.explanation: CSF passes from the lateral ventricles through the foramina of Monro into the third ventricle, then through the aqueduct of Sylvius into the fourth ventricle, and leaves through the apertures of Magendie and Luschka into the subarachnoid space.

ne-a1b6cd84.stem: In what order, from top to bottom, are the parts of the brainstem?
ne-a1b6cd84.explanation: From top to bottom the brainstem consists of the midbrain (mesencephalon), the pons and the medulla oblongata; the medulla continues as the spinal cord at the level of the foramen magnum.

ne-000ce129.stem: In which part of the brainstem are the vital centres for breathing and circulation?
ne-000ce129.explanation: The medulla oblongata contains the centres regulating breathing, heart rate and vascular tone. This is why compression of the medulla by herniation through the foramen magnum can be fatal.

ne-eb4c66bd.stem: Which structure is responsible for balance, muscle tone and the coordination of movements?
ne-eb4c66bd.explanation: The cerebellum regulates the timing and smoothness of movement and maintains balance and muscle tone. Damage causes ataxia, tremor and imbalance; the signs are on the same side as the lesion.

ne-3a99b000.stem: By how many pairs of peduncles is the cerebellum attached to the brainstem?
ne-3a99b000.explanation: The superior cerebellar peduncle connects to the midbrain, the middle to the pons and the inferior to the medulla oblongata. The largest is the middle peduncle, carrying fibres from the pons.

ne-64f89be2.stem: In adults, at what vertebral level does the spinal cord (conus medullaris) usually end?
ne-64f89be2.explanation: In adults the spinal cord ends with the conus medullaris at L1–L2; in the newborn it is lower, at about L3. Below it there are only nerve roots (the cauda equina).

ne-17d73e1a.stem: In what order, from outside inwards, are the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord?
options: Arachnoid mater – dura mater – pia mater
Dura mater – arachnoid mater – pia mater
Dura mater – pia mater – arachnoid mater
Pia mater – arachnoid mater – dura mater
Pia mater – dura mater – arachnoid mater
ne-17d73e1a.explanation: Outermost is the thick, tough dura mater, in the middle the web-like arachnoid, and innermost the thin pia mater, closely attached to the surface of the brain.

ne-904c7a31.stem: In which space does the cerebrospinal fluid circulate?
options: Between the two layers of the dura
Between the dura and the arachnoid (subdural space)
Between the pia mater and the brain tissue
Between the arachnoid and the pia mater (subarachnoid space)
Between the dura and the bone (epidural space)
ne-904c7a31.explanation: CSF circulates in the subarachnoid space, which widens into the cisterns. In lumbar puncture the needle enters this space to obtain CSF.

ne-4de7a681.stem: At which interspace is lumbar puncture usually performed in adults?
options: Between the L3–L4 or L4–L5 vertebrae
ne-4de7a681.explanation: Because the spinal cord ends at L1–L2, the needle is inserted lower, around the line joining the iliac crests (about L4); here there are only the roots of the cauda equina, which move away from the needle.

ne-407bca30.stem: What is the bundle of nerve roots descending in the vertebral canal below the conus medullaris called?
ne-407bca30.explanation: Because the spinal cord is shorter than the vertebral column, the lower lumbar and sacral roots descend to reach their foramina and form the cauda equina, which resembles a horse's tail. The filum terminale is a pial thread running from the conus to the coccyx.

ne-50ebda82.stem: How many pairs of cranial nerves are there?
ne-50ebda82.explanation: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain and brainstem, from I (olfactory) to XII (hypoglossal). There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves.

ne-ee88b313.stem: Which nerve supplies the muscle that raises the eyelid and most of the eye muscles?
ne-ee88b313.explanation: The oculomotor nerve supplies levator palpebrae superioris, the superior, inferior and medial recti and the inferior oblique; it also carries the parasympathetic fibres that constrict the pupil.

ne-b6c92d74.stem: Which nerve supplies lateral rectus (the muscle that turns the eye outwards)?
ne-b6c92d74.explanation: The abducens nerve supplies only lateral rectus. When it is paralysed the eye cannot be turned outwards and there is double vision on looking to the side (in short: LR6, SO4, the rest III).

ne-994f4b2e.stem: Which nerve carries sensation from the skin of the face and supplies the muscles of mastication?
ne-994f4b2e.explanation: The three divisions of the trigeminal nerve (ophthalmic, maxillary, mandibular) carry sensation from the skin of the face; the mandibular division also supplies the muscles of mastication such as masseter, temporalis and the pterygoids.

ne-252939b1.stem: Which nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression?
ne-252939b1.explanation: All the muscles that produce facial expression are supplied by the facial nerve. The muscles of mastication are supplied by the trigeminal nerve; this distinction is often confused.

ne-347049b5.stem: What is the motor nerve of the tongue muscles (except palatoglossus)?
ne-347049b5.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve supplies all the intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue; only palatoglossus is supplied by the vagus. In a one-sided palsy the protruded tongue deviates towards the paralysed side.
